| Topock, Arizona (US) | 121°F |
| Warsaw, Poland (Europe) | 101°F |
| Washington, DC (US) | 103°F |

What is the mean of the temperatures listed above if the lowest temperature is removed? Express your answer as a decimal to the nearest tenth. What is the positive difference between the means with and without the lowest temperature?

solutions.title: Recompute
solutions.body:
The mean of all ten is $1033 \div 10 = 103.3$. Removing 77: $(1033 - 77) \div 9 = 956 \div 9 \approx 106.2$°F. Difference: $106.2 - 103.3 = 2.9$.

**Answer: 106.2°F; difference 2.9°F**

solutions.title: Effect of removing one value
solutions.body:
Removing a value $x$ from $n$ values with mean $m$ changes the mean by $\frac{m - x}{n - 1} = \frac{103.3 - 77}{9} = \frac{26.3}{9} \approx 2.92$. New mean $\approx 103.3 + 2.92 \approx 106.2$.

**Answer: 106.2°F; difference 2.9°F**

prompt: The highest temperature ever recorded in Laughlin, Nevada was 125°F in June 1994. The highest temperature recorded there so far in 2026 is 114°F. What is the percent decrease between that record temperature and the highest temperature recorded there so far in 2026? Express your answer as a decimal to the nearest tenth.

solutions.title: Ratio
solutions.body:
$\frac{114}{125} = 0.912$, so 2026's high is 91.2% of the record — a decrease of $100 - 91.2 = 8.8\%$.

**Answer: 8.8%**
